q: 1. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called
explain: The constant difference of elevation between two consecutive contour lines is termed the contour interval.

q: 2. The V-shaped contour represents
explain: Contours crossing a stream or depression form V-shapes pointing upstream (toward higher ground), representing a valley; a ridge would show contours pointing away from higher ground (downhill).

q: 3. Straight, parallel and widely spaced contours represent
explain: Evenly, widely-spaced and straight/parallel contours indicate a uniformly sloping (inclined plane) surface; closely spaced contours indicate steep ground, and widely spaced but irregular contours indicate flatter, gently undulating ground.

q: 4. Contours of different elevations may cross each other only in the case of
explain: Normally contours of different elevations never cross; the sole exception is an overhanging cliff or cave, where the ground surface doubles back on itself, allowing contours of different elevations to appear to cross in plan.

q: 5. Closed contours of decreasing values towards their centre, represent
explain: When the innermost closed contour has the lowest elevation value, the feature represents a depression (a hollow); a hill is represented by closed contours of increasing value towards the centre.

q: 6. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called
explain: A line on the ground surface that maintains a constant inclination (gradient) to the horizontal throughout is called a contour gradient (grade contour), unlike a contour line which is horizontal (constant elevation).

q: 7. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient up hill side involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: When the actual road alignment on the uphill side deviates from (cuts across, rising faster than) the contour gradient, the road surface lies below the natural ground, requiring excavation along the centre line.

q: 8. The constant vertical distance between two adjacent contours, is called ...............
explain: Contour interval is the fixed vertical difference in elevation between any two consecutive contour lines.

q: 9. The contour interval is kept inversely proportional to ...............
options: time and expense of field work
steepness of the configuration of the area
explain: On steep ground, contours are close together, so a larger interval is used; on flat ground, a smaller interval is used to show detail.

q: 10. The direction of steepest slope on a contour, is ...............
options: at an angle of 45° to the contour
at right angles to the contour
explain: The shortest distance between two contours (the steepest path) is always the perpendicular distance between them.

q: 11. Two contour lines, having the same may cross each other only in the case of ...............
explain: According to the book's specific logic/key for this question, contours 'can cross' in the specific topographical anomaly of an overhanging cliff.

q: 12. The method generally preferred to for contouring an undulating area is,
explain: Tacheometric surveying, which can quickly determine both horizontal and vertical distances/elevations from a single setup, is best suited for contouring an undulating (hilly, uneven) area.

q: 13. Closed contours of decreasing values toward their centre, represent ...............
explain: If the elevation values decrease toward the center of closed loops, it indicates a hole, pond, or depression in the ground.

q: 14. Contours are used to determine
options: indivisibility of points on a contour map
area of the drainage basin and capacity of the reservoir
explain: Contour maps are versatile tools used to determine intervisibility of points, drainage basin areas and reservoir capacities, and earthwork quantities, so all listed uses apply.

q: 15. In route surveys, the most suitable method of contouring is
explain: For narrow, long projects like roads or railways, the cross-section method is the most efficient way to capture the topography.

q: 16. The horizontal equivalent which is a term generally uses in contoured map is .............
options: the least distance between two consecutive contours
the greatest distance between two consecutive contours
the mean distance between two consecutive contours
explain: Horizontal equivalent is the horizontal distance between two consecutive contours; it is smallest where the slope is steepest.

q: 17. A pass or a saddle in a mountainous region .............
options: the lowest point of the ridge lines coincides with the highest point of the valley point
explain: A saddle is a low point on a ridge between two peaks; it typically connects two ridges and two valleys.

q: 18. Which one of the following methods can be used for contour interpolation?
explain: Contour interpolation is done via estimation (rough), arithmetic (precise but slow), or graphical methods (using a tracing sheet).

q: 19. The contour interval depends upon the .............
explain: Contour intervals are chosen based on the steepness of terrain, the map scale, and the required precision for the project's purpose.

q: 20. In direct method of contouring, the process of locating or identifying points lying on a contour called .............
explain: Vertical control is the process used to find points of the same elevation (the contour line) using a level and staff.

q: 21. An imaginary line on the surface of the earth having a constant inclination with the horizontal (slope) is called
explain: As defined earlier, an imaginary line on the ground maintaining a constant slope (inclination to horizontal) is called a contour gradient.

q: 22. Contour lines cross ridge or valley lines at
explain: As established earlier, contour lines always cross ridge lines and valley lines at right angles (90 degrees), since these lines represent the direction of steepest slope.

q: 23. Contour interval is
options: inversely proportional to the scale of the map
directly proportional to the flatness of ground
larger if the time available is more
explain: A larger map scale (more detailed) generally uses a smaller contour interval and vice versa, so the contour interval is inversely proportional to the scale of the map.

q: 24. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation of contours is
explain: Interpolating contour positions between spot levels by arithmetical (proportional) calculation is considered the most accurate method, though graphical and estimation methods are quicker alternatives.

q: 25. A series of closely spaced contour lines represents a .............
explain: Close contours indicate that the elevation is changing rapidly over a short horizontal distance, signifying a steep slope.

q: 26. Direct method of contouring is .............
explain: The direct method involves physically tracing the contour on the ground; it is very accurate but slow and tedious.

q: 27. In case of double line river, contours are .............
options: stopped at the banks of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
drawn by parabolic curves having their vertex at the centre of the water
explain: For a double-line river, contours are drawn to the edge of the water but not across it, as the water surface itself is level.

q: 28. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from .............
explain: Starting from a saddle or ridge allows the surveyor to work downwards and find the best alignment for a road gradient.

q: 29. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient uphill side, involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: If the road is shifted towards the uphill side of the proposed contour gradient, it necessitates cutting into the hill (excavation).

q: 30. Two hill tops A and B 20 km apart are intervened by a third top C. If the top most contour of the three hill tops are of the same value, state whether the line of sight AB
options: passes below the hill top C
passes below the hill top C
explain: Due to the earth's curvature, the line of sight between two points at the same elevation will pass below the actual ground level of an intervening point of that same elevation.

q: 31. The best method of interpolation of contours, is by
explain: Interpolation by arithmetical calculation (computation) is the most accurate method, though it is slower than estimation or graphical methods.

q: 32. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation if contours .............
explain: Arithmetical calculation is the most accurate method for interpolation, as it assumes a uniform slope between points and calculates the exact position of the contour line.

q: 33. When several contours coincide, it indicates .............
explain: Contours coincide to form a single line only in the case of a vertical cliff.
